cover.headline: A science-led mid-cap whose growth now comes mostly from abroad: on the street's P/E method, with the multiple re-rated like the sector's, we see {{dcf.upside|chg}}
cover.lead: Emcure (FY26 revenue ₹9,204 cr) is two businesses: a #13-ranked Indian branded franchise (44%; iron, chiral cardiac molecules, Tenectase, plus Sanofi, Novo Nordisk and Roche brands it distributes) and generics front ends in Europe and Canada with an ARV tender business in emerging markets (56%). Q1FY27 revenue rose 22.8% (international +34.2% with ~12pp from the rupee, India +10.2%), EBITDA 26% and profit 36%; Bain has exited and the subsidiaries are now wholly owned. We forecast EPS of ₹60.0 / 73.5 / 87.3 for FY27-29E, ~5% below the bulls for FY28 because we assume no currency tailwind. Every broker that discloses a method uses **P/E**, and so do we: **27x Sep-28E EPS (₹80.4)**, i.e. Emcure's 23.3x median forward P/E since Jan-2025 lifted 16% for the pharma sector's re-rating over the same window, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,267; DCF ₹1,548. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Real chemistry, a few category leaders
arguments.p: Chiral cardiac molecules, the Orofer iron family (#1 in iron combinations), Tenectase (100% share) and the first EU generic of liposomal amphotericin B: ~50% of India revenue and ~30% of international revenue come from complex products, and 30-35% of India sales from in-house R&D. #2 in gynaecology. This is a better business than a #13 rank suggests.

arguments.h: But recent growth is borrowed or cyclical
arguments.p: India grew 10.2% in Q1FY27, only 6-7% without the in-licensed Sanofi and Roche brands, after a Zuventus restructuring hit Q4FY26. International (+34.2%) carried the quarter on ARV tenders (two-thirds of rest of world) and a weaker rupee (6-7pp of group growth). Gross margin fell 340bp to 58.4% on that mix.

Bain sold its last shares in Jun-2026; Zuventus (₹725 cr) and Gennova (₹232 cr, from its CEO, ~₹1,924 cr implied for a ₹5 cr-profit company) are now 100% owned. The founder becomes Chairman too and his son COO. ₹276 cr of sales to the promoters' US company with ₹197 cr outstanding, and a pending ~2.8% promoter sale to meet the public-float rule, argue against a premium. Net debt ₹1,054 cr (0.6x EBITDA), ~nil by Mar-28E on our numbers.

At ₹1,943 the stock is 36.4x trailing and 26.4x our FY28E EPS, against a 23.3x forward median since Jan-2025: it has re-rated with the sector (trailing P/E +4% vs its own median; peers +16%). Our 27x sits inside the street's 24-30x. The DCF (₹1,548) says cash flow, held back by working capital, does not support the price on its own.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): India growth vs the market (Zuventus), gross margin as Europe and ARV grow, net debt after the July payouts (~₹1,450 cr guided).
Promoter sale or share issue to take public shareholding to 25% (~2.8% of equity; on our reading due by Jul-2027).
Launches abroad: liposomal amphotericin B tenders across Europe, semaglutide in Canada (Dr. Reddy's supply in Quebec; own filing), lenacapavir registration (FY27).
Poviztra traction after the Apr-2026 price cut and the Jul-2026 MASH approval; Roche and Sanofi diabetes brands in the base from Q2FY27.
AR FY27 related-party note: the Avet receivable (₹197 cr at Mar-26) and the Gennova payment terms.

sections.title: A US$1 bn Pune drug maker: a mid-sized Indian brand business (44%) plus generics fronts in Europe and Canada and an ARV tender business (56%)

blocks.p: Emcure develops, makes and sells medicines in two very different ways. **In India (44% of FY26 revenue)** it sells branded generics to doctors through ~4,000 medical representatives: #13 in the Indian market, #2 in gynaecology, strongest in women's health (the Orofer iron franchise), cardiology (its own chiral molecules plus Sanofi's Cardace, Clexane and Lasilactone, distributed since Mar-2024), diabetes (Sanofi's Amaryl and Cetapin since 2025, Novo Nordisk's semaglutide brand Poviztra since Nov-2025), CNS (Tenectase for stroke) and oncology/nephrology. About 15% of India sales are in-licensed MNC brands. **Abroad (56%)** it sells generics through its own subsidiaries: Tillomed in the UK and Europe (20% of revenue; complex injectables such as liposomal amphotericin B), Marcan and Mantra in Canada (16%; a top-10 generic company), and in 80+ emerging markets (20%), where roughly half is anti-HIV (ARV) medicines sold in tenders. It does not sell in the US (that business was demerged to a promoter-owned company in 2020-21). Manufacturing is in 13 Indian plants, with in-house APIs and biologics (Gennova).

blocks.callout: **So what:** Emcure is a mix of a mid-sized Indian brand business (good, but sub-scale against the top-10 players and growing at market pace) and an international generics platform that has been the growth engine for three years. The international half earns lower gross margins and grows in lumps (tenders, launches, currency). Investors are paying for both; the street usually values the whole on P/E as if it were an Indian branded company.

sections.title: From a 1981 Pune start-up to a 2024 IPO: private equity for a decade, a US exit, and a run of buyouts since listing

blocks.p: Satish Mehta founded Emcure in 1981 and entered Indian branded generics in 1995. Subsidiaries Gennova (biotech) and Zuventus (acute brands) were set up in 2001-02 with outside shareholders. Blackstone invested in 2006; Bain Capital bought its ~13% stake in 2013-14 for ~₹700 cr. Emcure expanded abroad by acquisition: Tillomed (UK, 2014), Marcan (Canada, 2015) and Mantra (Quebec, 2023). Its US business (Heritage, now Avet) was demerged to a promoter-owned company in 2020-21 together with the US drug-pricing litigation. An IPO filed in 2021 was not pursued; the Jul-2024 IPO raised ₹800.6 cr of new money and let Bain and the promoters sell 1.14 cr shares. Since listing, Emcure has bought out the minorities in Zuventus and Gennova and added three in-licensing deals (Sanofi diabetes, Novo Nordisk, Roche).

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the history explains today's structure. Private equity backed a founder-led company for 18 years and has now exited; the US business and its legal problems sit with the promoters, not with Emcure, but a commercial link remains (Emcure sold ₹276 cr of products to Avet in FY26). The post-IPO priority has been control (100% of every subsidiary) and distribution deals with MNCs, rather than large new platforms.

sections.title: Three markets: Indian branded generics (~10% growth), regulated-market generics in Europe and Canada (low growth, price deflation), and donor-funded ARV tenders

blocks.p: **India.** The domestic formulations market was ₹2.57 lakh cr in FY26 (+9.9%, IQVIA); growth comes from price (4-5% a year, capped for essential drugs), new products and low-single-digit volume. Emcure expects 8-9% industry growth in FY27; the market grew 13.0% in Q1FY27 (excluding tirzepatide). Two shifts matter for Emcure: chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes) gain share, and multinationals increasingly hand mature brands to Indian partners with larger field forces (Sanofi, Novo Nordisk and Roche all chose Emcure). Semaglutide went off patent in Mar-2026 and 40-50 generic brands launched. **Europe and Canada.** Generic markets of US$70 bn+ (Europe) where the money is in hard-to-make products (complex injectables, first generics); plain generics face steady price erosion. Emcure has its own front ends in the UK, Italy and Canada. **Rest of world.** Anti-HIV medicines bought in large tenders (Global Fund, governments) at thin prices, plus branded generics in 80+ countries; the next leg is long-acting HIV prevention (lenacapavir, monthly pills) under voluntary licences.

bullets: **Covered-market share and brands per doctor are below peers** (Kotak's question on the Q1FY27 call); management's answer is in-licensing to raise co-prescription.
**In-licensed brands grow with the market, not faster** (management, Aug-2026), and they are distribution rights: Sanofi's cardiac deal has an initial term of five years from Mar-2024.
**GLP-1s:** Emcure sells the innovator's rDNA semaglutide (Poviztra) against 40-50 cheaper synthetic generics; price cut in Apr-2026; MASH indication added in Jul-2026; revenue not disclosed.
**Currency:** a weaker rupee lifts international revenue (6-7pp of group growth in Q1FY27) and produced ₹119 cr of exchange gains in FY26; management assumes ₹92/US$ for FY27.

blocks.callout: **So what:** none of Emcure's markets is a high-growth one on its own. Growth has to come from share gains: launches of hard-to-make products abroad, in-licensed brands and field-force productivity at home. That makes execution, not the industry, the main driver of the numbers.

sections.title: Does the sector tailwind reach Emcure? Abroad, yes (and the rupee helps); in India, only at market pace after a messy Zuventus year

blocks.p: India grew 10% in FY26, broadly in line with the market, but the quality was mixed: the Sanofi diabetes brands (from Q2FY26) and Roche (from Apr-2026) added growth, while Zuventus, the acute-focused subsidiary with ~40% of the field force, shrank after the minority buyout (Oct-2025), the founder-CEO's exit and a restructuring that drove attrition. India grew only 5.2% in Q4FY26. Q1FY27 was +10.2%, about 6-7% excluding Sanofi diabetes and Roche; management promises market-pace growth in Q2 and faster growth in H2 on a weak base. International grew 22% in FY26 and 34% in Q1FY27 (~21% in constant currency), on liposomal amphotericin B in Europe, share gains in Canada and the ARV order book.

sections.title: India: strong brands in iron, cardiac chirals and stroke; growth now leans on Sanofi, Novo and Roche brands while Zuventus recovers

blocks.p: India revenue was ₹4,027 cr in FY26 (+10%): FY24 ₹3,144 cr, FY25 ₹3,660 cr (+16%, the first year of the Sanofi cardiac brands). Emcure's own franchise is built on products from its R&D (30-35% of India sales): the Orofer iron family (ferrous ascorbate and ferric carboxymaltose, #1 in iron combinations), chiral cardiac molecules (Metpure, Numlo, Asomex, "lower dose and better safety"), Tenectase (tenecteplase for stroke and heart attack, 100% share, ~24% CAGR FY22-26), Pause, Bevon and Maxtra. Women's health and cardio-metabolics are ~50% of India sales. On top sit in-licensed MNC brands (~15% of India sales): Sanofi's cardiac range (Cardace, Clexane, Lasilactone, Targocid, Lasix) since Mar-2024, its diabetes brands Amaryl and Cetapin since 2025, Novo Nordisk's Poviztra since Nov-2025 and Roche's nephrology/transplant brands from Apr-2026. Zuventus, the acute-focused subsidiary (₹1,041 cr revenue in FY26, −4%), is the weak spot: after the minority buyout (Oct-2025) and its founder-CEO's exit, a restructuring in Q4FY26 drove high attrition and India grew only 5.2% in the quarter.

sections.title: Europe and Canada: own front ends and a complex-injectables pipeline; 20%+ growth helped by the rupee, mid-teens without it

blocks.p: **Europe (Tillomed)** grew from ₹1,411 cr (FY24) to ₹1,850 cr (FY26, +25.5%) and ₹537 cr in Q1FY27 (+32.8%, of which ~12pp currency). Emcure sells hospital and retail generics directly in the UK and Italy and through partners elsewhere. Growth drivers are liposomal amphotericin B (the first EU generic of a ~US$270 mn product; tendered in "pretty much all" EU countries, supplies ramping), the Manx portfolio bought in 2025 (120+ marketing authorisations) and a 55+ product pipeline (ferric carboxymaltose, liposomal doxorubicin next). Management expects mid-teens CAGR over two years. **Canada (Marcan, Mantra)** grew from ₹923 cr (FY24) to ₹1,487 cr (FY26, +18.7%) and ₹427 cr in Q1FY27 (+24.6%): a top-10 generic company with a pan-Canadian front end since Mantra (Quebec, 2023), present in hospital, retail and OTC, with 50+ products in development and 8 near-term first-generic opportunities. Semaglutide is the most visible: Mantra will sell Dr. Reddy's generic in Quebec (timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply) and Emcure is filing its own.

sections.title: Rest of world: an ARV tender business that is growing fast but lumpy, plus branded generics in 80+ countries

blocks.p: Rest-of-world revenue grew from ₹1,181 cr (FY24) to ₹1,840 cr (FY26, +21.8%) and ₹522 cr in Q1FY27 (+44.8%). Two businesses sit here. **ARV** (anti-HIV medicines for Africa and Latin America, sold in large tenders) was about two-thirds of the region in Q1FY27 and should be 50-55% for the year (management); Emcure competes on cost (backward integration into APIs) and holds voluntary licences for Gilead's twice-yearly lenacapavir (one of six licensees; DMF filed, registration expected in FY27) and, since Jul-2026, MSD's once-monthly oral PrEP candidate (royalty-free, 129 countries). **Non-ARV** branded generics are sold directly in Kenya, South Africa, Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Peru, the Philippines and the Dominican Republic and through partners elsewhere (15+ approvals in Q1FY27, 3 new territories).

blocks.callout: **Verdict: narrow moat at best.** Emcure's genuine edge is in chemistry and complex manufacturing (chiral molecules, iron, liposomal injectables, biologics), which gives it first-to-market products in India and first generics abroad. Its brands lead in a handful of categories. But it is a mid-sized player in India, its fastest-growing domestic products are other companies' brands on time-limited distribution deals, and more than half of revenue is generics and tenders where advantages erode. We do not pay a premium for the moat; the multiple we use is the stock's own history adjusted only for the sector.

sections.title: Revenue ×2 in seven years and margins up from 14% to 19%; EPS stalled in FY23-24 and has compounded since the IPO cut the debt

blocks.p: Emcure's revenue grew from ₹4,717 cr in FY19 to ₹9,204 cr in FY26 (10% a year), but unevenly: +7% in FY20, flat in FY21 (the year the US business was demerged), +16% in FY22, flat in FY23, then +11% / +19% / +17% in FY24-26 as the Sanofi cardiac brands (from Mar-2024), Mantra in Canada (Nov-2023) and new launches in Europe and the rest of the world kicked in. EBITDA margin rose from 14-16% before FY21 to 23-24% in FY21-22 and has settled at 18-20% since FY23 (FY26 19.4% on the company basis). **Profit is where the change shows.** Profit to shareholders fell from ₹662 cr in FY22 to ₹498 cr in FY24 (higher interest, depreciation and a weaker margin), then rose to ₹681 cr in FY25 and ₹924 cr in FY26 (EPS ₹48.8; ₹52.1 before exceptional items and the ₹42.9 cr Mantra earn-out true-up) as IPO money repaid debt, the margin improved and foreign-exchange gains (₹119 cr) helped. We forecast EPS of ₹60.0 / 73.5 / 87.3 for FY27-29E.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounting, but weak cash conversion, currency gains in profit and three EBITDA definitions to reconcile

bullets: **Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was ₹944 cr in FY26, 53% of company EBITDA (FY24 89%, FY25 58%): working capital absorbed ₹530 cr as inventory and receivables rose ₹1,027 cr. Inventory + receivables − payables is 34% of revenue. This is the main quality issue.

**Currency gains.** FY26 profit included ₹119 cr of foreign-exchange gains (9% of PBT; ₹23 cr in Q1FY27) as the rupee fell. The company's "adjusted PAT" keeps them. We forecast none, which is one reason our FY27E EPS growth looks modest against FY26.

**Three EBITDA numbers.** Company ₹1,789 cr (19.4%, excludes exchange gains and the ₹42.9 cr earn-out true-up); Screener ₹1,746 cr (19.0%, includes the true-up as a cost); ICICI Direct ₹1,907 cr (includes exchange gains). Screener's quarterly operating profit includes exchange gains (Q1FY27 ₹532 cr vs company ₹508 cr). We forecast on the company basis.

**Exceptional items.** FY26 −₹31.4 cr (labour codes ₹26.1 cr, a legal settlement ₹3.5 cr, consultancy ₹1.8 cr) plus the ₹42.9 cr Mantra earn-out true-up booked above the line; FY25 −₹10.4 cr (US and EU legal settlements) and a ₹38.2 cr gain on asset sales in other income.
**Traded goods.** Purchases of finished products rose 27% to ₹2,397 cr (26% of revenue), mostly the Sanofi brands; these carry distribution margins, not brand margins.
**Related-party sales.** ₹276 cr of sales to the promoter-owned US company Avet and its units in FY26, with ₹197 cr receivable at Mar-26 (Avet ₹167 cr, about 266 days of its purchases).

**Contingent liabilities.** ₹259 cr incl. interest (income tax ₹100 cr after the Dec-2020 search; indirect tax ₹64 cr); US price-fixing cases indemnified by Avet; a Canadian class action against Marcan being settled.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** We see nothing aggressive in revenue recognition, and the auditor (B S R & Co., KPMG network) gave a clean opinion. But profit has run ahead of cash for two years, currency gains flattered FY26, and the related-party receivable from Avet is large relative to the sales. We show reported EPS and EPS before exceptional items side by side and forecast no currency gains.

sections.title: Net debt: ₹1,558 cr before the IPO, ₹434 cr after it, ₹1,054 cr after the Zuventus buyout; on our path ~nil by Mar-28 and net cash by Mar-29

blocks.p: Gross borrowings were ₹1,204 cr at Mar-26 against ₹150 cr of cash and liquid investments: net debt ₹1,054 cr (0.6x EBITDA), excluding ₹317 cr of lease liabilities and the ₹336 cr Mantra earn-out payable. Most of the debt is short-term working-capital finance (₹795 cr), plus a ₹194 cr rupee term loan (raised in FY26, secured on plant and brands) and ₹212 cr of Canadian-dollar term loans at Mantra and Marcan guaranteed by the parent. Net debt was ₹1,103 cr at Jun-26 and rose to ~₹1,560 cr in August after the July payouts (Mantra ₹336 cr, Gennova ₹232 cr); the CFO expects ~₹1,450 cr at Sep-26 and net cash by end-FY28. Our path, which adds the Gennova and Cutimed payments and lease principal (~₹55 cr a year) that the engine does not see, gives net debt of ₹1,064 cr at Mar-27, ₹204 cr at Mar-28 and net cash of ₹881 cr at Mar-29.

blocks.p: Satish Mehta (founder, MD & CEO since 1981) will also be Chairman after the 2026 AGM, when Berjis Desai, a lawyer who chaired the board and worked with him for 35 years, retires. sections.title: Valuation: 27x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the stock has already re-rated with the sector

blocks.p: Every note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method values Emcure on **P/E**: ICICI Direct 30x FY28E EPS (4-Sep-2026), Motilal Oswal 28x 12-month-forward EPS (7-Aug-2026), BOB Capital Markets 25x Mar-28E EPS (6-May-2026) and JM Financial 24x Sep-27E EPS (Nov-2025). We follow them: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, the earnings a buyer will look at one year from now. EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks, not weights. Forecasts carry no exceptional items or currency gains, so the multiple applies directly to model EPS.

Emcure listed on 10-Jul-2024, so there is no five-year history. Following the batch rule (PLAYBOOK §7c), we use its own one-year-forward P/E **since 1-Jan-2025**, skipping the IPO months (Jul-Dec 2024, median 26.3x), on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (92 points): price ÷ the next full fiscal year's EPS (FY26 actual before exceptional items and the earn-out true-up, then our FY27-28E). We multiply the median by the nine-peer pharma factor measured over the **same window** (+16%) and round to the nearest half-turn. No own move, growth or returns adjustment enters the base; those are sensitivities below.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than its #13 rank suggests, priced for it; we would buy below ~₹1,890

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** real chemistry and complex-product skills (chiral molecules, iron, liposomal injectables, biologics), category-leading brands in women's health and stroke, a distribution platform MNCs want to partner with, and generics front ends in Europe and Canada growing 20%; a balance sheet that will be close to net cash by FY28E. **What you are not buying:** a top-10 India franchise, owned brands for most of the recent India growth, or a business with high, stable margins (19-20% EBITDA, gross margin falling with mix).

**What you are paying:** ₹1,943 is 36.4x trailing EPS and 26.4x our FY28E EPS (24.2x Sep-28E), against a 23.3x median one-year-forward P/E since Jan-2025. The stock has re-rated with the sector: its trailing P/E is +4% vs its own median since Jan-2025, the nine pharma peers +16%. On the street's method (P/E) with our derived 27x Sep-28E EPS, the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a HOLD. The EV/EBITDA cross-check (₹2,267) agrees; the DCF (₹1,548 at 11.9%) does not, as for most of the sector: the price assumes long, high growth.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Emcure Pharmaceuticals (consolidated, ₹ crore), as of 30-Sep-2026 on Q1FY27 results (6-Aug-2026). Net Profit is profit attributable to owners (EMCURE.patch.js); Zuventus has been wholly owned since 3-Oct-2025 and Gennova since Jul-2026, so forecasts carry no minorities. One reportable segment (pharmaceuticals) with four geographies (India, Europe, Canada, rest of world), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the geography build sits in `businessLines` and EMCURE.ctx.js checks it sums to model revenue. EBITDA is on the company's definition (excluding other income, foreign-exchange gains and the Mantra earn-out true-up); Screener's FY26 operating profit (₹1,746 cr, 19.0%) is ₹43 cr below the company's ₹1,789 cr (19.4%) because Screener books the ₹42.86 cr earn-out true-up in expenses. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS (every broker that discloses a method uses P/E: Motilal Oswal, ICICI Direct, BOB Capital Markets, JM Financial), with the multiple derived per PLAYBOOK §7c (own forward median since 1-Jan-2025 × the same-window pharma factor); EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the geography build below on FY26 revenue of ₹9,204 cr (company: India ₹4,027 cr, Europe ₹1,850 cr, Canada ₹1,487 cr, rest of world ₹1,840 cr). FY27E ₹10,550 cr (+14.6%): management guided 'low to mid-teen' growth and on 6-Aug-2026 said it was 'more comfortable being at the higher end'; Q1FY27 was +22.8% with ~6-7pp from the weaker rupee (management assumes ₹92 to the dollar on average for FY27). India +10.5% (Q1 +10.2%, about 6-7% excluding the in-licensed Sanofi diabetes and Roche brands; management expects market-pace growth in Q2 and faster in H2 on a weak Q4FY26 base hit by the Zuventus restructuring; industry growth expected at 8-9%). Europe +18% (Q1 +32.8% incl. ~12-13pp currency; liposomal amphotericin B tenders and the Manx portfolio; management sees mid-teens CAGR over two years). Canada +15% (Q1 +24.6%; share gains, new launches, Cutimed; semaglutide via Dr. Reddy's in Quebec not counted). Rest of world +20% (Q1 +44.8%, ARV two-thirds of the region in the quarter, normalising to 50-55% for the year). FY28-29E: India +11% / +10.5% (market ~9-10% plus chronic and in-licensed brands), Europe +13% / +12%, Canada +12% / +11%, rest of world +12% / +11%, with no further currency tailwind. We are ~2pp below the street's FY28E growth (Motilal Oswal +14.3%, ICICI Direct +13.9%).

businessLines._why: FY26 by geography from the Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 investor presentations (₹ mn ÷ 10). Growth rates are explained in _revenueWhy.

assumptions._marginWhy: Company EBITDA definition (before other income, foreign-exchange gains and the earn-out true-up): FY24 18.5%, FY25 18.6%, FY26 19.4% (Screener 19.0% after the ₹42.86 cr Mantra earn-out true-up), Q1FY27 19.7% (+50bp) even as gross margin fell 340bp to 58.4% on the shift to Europe and ARV. FY27E 20.2% = FY26's 19.4% plus 80bp, inside management's 70-100bp (Q1FY27 call; 75-100bp in May) guidance, with gross margin guided to ~59% and R&D to 4-5% of revenue (3.5% in Q1, to rise). FY28-29E +60bp / +40bp from operating leverage on a field force whose productivity rose from ₹5.4 lakh to ₹7.0 lakh a month per rep in two years, employee costs growing ~10% against revenue +11-12%, partly offset by a lower-margin international mix. We are below Motilal Oswal (20.4% / 21.7%). Each 1pp of margin is ~₹118 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹4.6 of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Management guided FY27 capex at '₹400 crores rough number... ₹400-425-ish crores' (Q4FY26 call, May-2026); company capex was ₹276 / 376 / 488 cr in FY24-26 (cash: PP&E ₹361 cr plus intangibles ₹187 cr in FY26) and ₹95 cr in Q1FY27. FY27E ₹425 cr (top of guidance), then ₹460 cr and ₹500 cr (~3.9% and 3.8% of revenue) for complex injectables, biosimilars and dossiers. Acquisitions (Gennova minority ₹232 cr and Cutimed up to ₹34 cr in FY27) are not capex; EMCURE.ctx.js deducts them in our own net-debt path.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹415 cr = 7.3% of average gross block (₹5,695 cr incl. intangibles and right-of-use assets): PP&E ₹256 cr, right-of-use ₹53 cr, intangibles ₹106 cr (AR FY26 note 35). Q1FY27 ₹110 cr (₹440 cr annualised). 7.25% gives ₹447 / 479 / 514 cr. CWIP (₹273 cr) is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash, which is negative until FY29E. Treasury income on gross cash is built in otherIncome instead (EMCURE.ctx.js).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 30; checked in EMCURE.ctx.js). FY26 other income was only ₹12.66 cr: interest ₹1.68 cr, fund gains ₹1.52 cr, miscellaneous ₹9.46 cr (one-time licence income, sundry balances written back, rent, insurance claims). FY25 ₹67.26 cr included ₹38.24 cr of profit on asset sales, a leasehold-land gain and interest on the IPO money (₹9.04 cr). Forecast: (1) treasury income at 2% on ~₹150 cr of operating cash plus 6.5% on any surplus cash once net debt is repaid; (2) recurring miscellaneous income (rent, scrap, write-backs, insurance) ₹6 cr a year. Not forecast: foreign-exchange gains (₹118.80 cr in FY26 as the rupee fell; ₹23 cr in Q1FY27), which Screener's annual table counts as other income, and one-offs. Twelve months to Jun-26 (Screener, excl. exchange gains): ₹11 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on borrowings (working-capital loans, INR term loan, Canadian term loans), leases, other borrowing costs and the earn-out discount unwind
assumptions._interestWhy: Built from the debt path (AR FY26 notes 19-20 and 36; checked in EMCURE.ctx.js). FY26 finance cost ₹143.67 cr: interest on borrowings ₹73.94 cr (7.6% on ~₹968 cr of average gross debt), leases ₹26.75 cr, other borrowing costs ₹20.26 cr, unwinding of the Mantra earn-out discount ₹16.89 cr, interest on advance-tax shortfall ₹5.83 cr. Forecast: 7.5% on average gross borrowings from our net-debt path (gross debt ₹1,204 cr at Mar-26, ₹1,291 cr at Jun-26, up to ~₹1,600 cr after the July-2026 Mantra (₹336 cr) and Gennova (₹232 cr) payouts, then falling as free cash flow repays it; management targets net cash by end-FY28); leases ₹27 cr; other borrowing costs ₹18 cr; advance-tax interest ₹3 cr; earn-out unwind ₹5 cr in FY27 only (redeemed Jul-2026). Q1FY27 actual ₹32 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective rate 26.9% reported, 26% excluding exceptional items (CFO); Q1FY27 25.7%. India is on the 25.17% regime; Canada (~26.5%) and the UK (25%) are similar. FY27E 26.0%, then 25.8%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Emcure paid ₹57 cr of dividends in FY26 (₹3 a share, ~6% of profit). Cash goes first to the July-2026 payouts and debt reduction (net cash by end-FY28 guided). We assume a 6% payout.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity: 6.5% + 0.9 x 6% = 11.9%. Net debt (~₹1,450 cr expected at Sep-26 incl. the July payouts) is ~4% of a ~₹37,000 cr market value and is guided to nil by FY28, so WACC ≈ cost of equity; beta 0.9 (above a domestic branded peer's 0.8) for the 56% of revenue from tender-driven ARV and regulated-market generics and for the governance flags.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5% nominal: India (44% of revenue) grows 8-10% in value, Europe and Canada generics 3-6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from 11% to 7.5% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 22%: above the FY29E 21.2% as complex injectables and biosimilars scale, below the 25%+ of India-led peers because more than half of revenue is lower-margin international generics and ARV.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India returns to 1.2x the market as Zuventus accelerates and Poviztra scales, liposomal amphotericin B and semaglutide (Canada) win tenders and share, lenacapavir and the ARV order book keep the rest of world growing in high teens, and gross margin holds near 60%.

bear.narrative: Zuventus stays a laggard and India grows below the market, ARV tenders turn (pricing, donor funding) and European generics deflation returns, the rupee strengthens, and the Sanofi cardiac distribution deal (initial five years from Mar-2024) is renegotiated on worse terms.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Emcure: every note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method uses P/E (ICICI Direct 30x FY28E, 4-Sep-2026; Motilal Oswal 28x 12-month-forward EPS, 7-Aug-2026; BOB Capital Markets 25x Mar-28E, 6-May-2026; JM Financial 24x Sep-27E, Nov-2025). 27x Sep-28E EPS: Emcure's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Jan-2025 (listed 10-Jul-2024; IPO months skipped; 92 weekly closes plus the 30-Sep close; FY26 EPS before exceptional items and the ₹42.86 cr earn-out true-up = ₹52.1, then our FY27-28E), 23.3x, × 1.160 (nine pharma peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window: +16.0%, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +16.0%) = 27.0x, nearest half-turn 27x. Bull 29x / bear 25.5x = 75th / 25th percentiles × 1.160. On reported EPS the median is 23.3x (sensitivity). Forecasts carry no exceptional items, so the engine applies the multiple to its own Sep-28E EPS. Checked in EMCURE.ctx.js; written by EMCURE.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check. Emcure's median trailing EV/EBITDA since 1-Jan-2025 (Screener, 91 weekly points) is 17.0x; × 1.108 (the nine peers' EV/EBITDA move against their medians over the same window: +10.8%, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +10.8%) = 18.8x → 19x, applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) less net debt at Sep-27E (engine basis, incl. leases). Bull 20.5x / bear 18x = 75th / 25th percentiles × 1.108.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 11.9% (cost of equity ≈ WACC: net debt is small and guided to nil by FY28), terminal growth 5.5%; less net debt at Mar-27 (engine, incl. the Mantra earn-out paid in Jul-2026).

otherTreasury.label: Debt-like: Mantra earn-out payable (CAD 50.23 mn, redeemed Jul-2026) inside other liabilities
otherTreasury._why: Engine workaround. At Mar-26 Screener's other liabilities include the CAD 50.23 mn (₹335.77 cr) owed to Mantra's former shareholders for the earn-out, redeemed in July 2026 (AR FY26 note 63). It is deferred acquisition consideration, i.e. debt-like, not working capital. This entry takes it out of working capital (owc 33.1% of FY26 sales instead of 29.5%, close to the company's inventory + receivables − payables of 34%) and adds it to net debt in the engine and the Excel alike, so the July payout is not missed.
